items.label: Written for 12MAG (Claude, modelled on Cambridge Example 19)
items.text: The number of bottles of sunscreen sold at a beach kiosk and the daily maximum temperature are linearly related, with r = +0.912. Determine the value of the coefficient of determination, write it in percentage terms and interpret. In this relationship, daily maximum temperature is the explanatory variable.
items.answer: r² = (0.912)² = 0.8317; 83.2% of the variation in the number of bottles of sunscreen sold can be explained by the variation in the daily maximum temperature.

items.label: Written for 12MAG (Claude, modelled on Cambridge Example 20)
items.text: Scores on tests of reading speed and spelling ability are linearly related with correlation coefficient r = +0.342. Determine the value of the coefficient of determination, write it in percentage terms, and interpret. In this relationship, reading speed is the explanatory variable.
items.answer: r² = (0.342)² = 0.1170; only 11.7% of the variation in spelling ability test scores can be explained by the variation in reading speed test scores.

items.label: Written for 12MAG (Claude, modelled on Cambridge Example 21)
items.text: For the relationship described by this scatterplot, the coefficient of determination = 0.6384. Determine the value of the correlation coefficient, r, rounded to four decimal places.
items.figure: scatterplot showing a moderate-to-strong POSITIVE linear association (draw when the slides are made; keep it positive)
items.answer: r = ±√0.6384 = ±0.7990; the scatterplot shows a positive association, so r = +0.7990.

items.label: Written for 12MAG (Claude, modelled on Cambridge Example 2)
items.text:
Use the following information to find the value of the correlation coefficient r, rounded to three decimal places.
hours of sleep: mean 7.42, standard deviation 2.05 · reaction test score: mean 61.8, standard deviation 9.42
least squares equation: reaction test score = 38.2 + 3.18 × hours of sleep
items.answer: EV: hours of sleep (x), RV: reaction test score (y). b = 3.18, s_x = 2.05, s_y = 9.42. r = b × s_x / s_y = 3.18 × 2.05 / 9.42 = 0.692.

items.label: Written for 12MAG (Claude, modelled on Cambridge Example 5)
items.text:
In a recent study of a group of schools the correlation between Year 12 study score and hours of paid work per week was found to be −0.45, whilst the correlation between Year 12 study score and hours of sleep per night was found to be 0.31.
a Find the values of the coefficient of determination between Year 12 study score and hours of paid work per week, and hours of sleep per night respectively.
b Which of the variables, hours of paid work per week or hours of sleep per night, is more important in explaining the variation in Year 12 study score?
items.answer: a hours of paid work: r² = (−0.45)² = 20.3%; hours of sleep: r² = 0.31² = 9.6%. b Hours of paid work per week, because it explains a larger percentage of the variation in Year 12 study score (20.3% compared with 9.6%).

items.label: Written for 12MAG (Claude, modelled on Cambridge Example 8)
items.text:
Construct a report to describe the association between the price and age of secondhand motorbikes.
age (years): 1 2 2 3 4 5 5 6 7 8
price ($): 14 800 13 900 13 100 12 600 11 200 10 500 9800 9300 8100 7400
items.figure: scatterplot of price against age with the least squares line, and the residual plot (residuals 203, 372, −428, 141, −191, 178, −522, 47, −84, 285: no clear pattern). Draw both from the data when the slides are made.
items.answer: From the scatterplot we see that there is a strong negative, linear association between the price of a secondhand motorbike and its age, r = −0.993. There are no obvious outliers. The equation of the least squares regression line is: price = 15 700 − 1070 × age. The slope of the regression line predicts that, on average, the price of these secondhand motorbikes decreased by $1070 each year. The intercept predicts that, on average, the price of these motorbikes when new was $15 700. The coefficient of determination indicates that 98.5% of the variation in the price of these secondhand motorbikes is explained by the variation in their age. The lack of a clear pattern in the residual plot confirms the assumption of a linear association between the price and the age of these secondhand motorbikes.
